newsitem.title: USA: Archer proposes changing US tax plan to retain AMT.
newsitem.headline: Archer proposes changing US tax plan to retain AMT.

text.p: Big U.S. companies would be subject to the alternative minimum tax under changes House Ways and Means Committee Chairman Bill Archer proposed to his tax cut legislation.
Under the amendments, released Wednesday evening as the House panel began considering tax reforms, the corporate AMT would be repealed only for small businesses.
But, small businesses that become large would be subject to the alternative tax for new transactions and businesses.

The Texas Republican initially proposed phasing in a repeal of the AMT for all corporations, to be finalized by 2006. Under the initial proposal, the phased in repeal would have cost the government more than $17 billion through 2002.
